newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hiccup ahead for Telecom - NZ Herald.
newsitem.headline: Hiccup ahead for Telecom - NZ Herald.

text.p: Telecom's golden profit run appears set to be broken, the New Zealand Herald newspaper reported on Thursday.
The Herald said problems were mounting with Telecom's loss-making Australian operation, Pacific Star.
"Earnings are expected to come in below expectation for the first time since listing five years ago, when its second-quarter profit is announced on November 14," the paper said.
"A profit of about NZ$185 million is now anticipated, down from the previous market expectations of $200 million for the September quarter."

The Herald understands only around $10 million of that shortfall relates to operating losses from Pacific Star. There was speculation that Telecom might make a provision of up to $50 million to cover the possible closure of the Australian operation.
The Herald said Telecom's chief executive, Roderick Deane, was believed to be in Australia assessing options.
Problems at Pacific Star were confirmed in July, when Telecom indicated it may sell out of the company.
Telecom spokesman Clive Litt told Reuters the company had a policy not to comment on profit forecasts.
